items.question_text:
The main site of alcohol metabolism is the:

a. spleen

b. kidney 

c. liver 

d. colon
items.answer_text:
Alcohol metabolism primarily takes place in the **liver**, where enzymes such as alcohol dehydrogenase and acetaldehyde dehydrogenase break down ethanol into acetaldehyde and then into acetic acid. This process helps to detoxify alcohol from the body. The liver is equipped to handle the metabolic load of alcohol, but excessive alcohol consumption can overwhelm its capacity, leading to liver damage and other health issues. Unlike the liver, the spleen, kidney, and colon do not play significant roles in alcohol metabolism. Therefore, the liver is considered the main site of alcohol metabolism in the body.

c. liver
